title: Understanding Price Action — practical study map

source.author: Bob Volman
source.title: Understanding Price Action: Practical Analysis of the 5-Minute Time Frame
source.printed_page_anchors: Used where available; PDF index differs because of front matter

caveat: Educational source notes. Not a trading signal, investment advice, or profitability claim.

concepts.name: Double pressure
concepts.definition: Directional movement recruits participants in the move while opposing traders exit or cover, increasing follow-through potential.
cues: break from defended level
follow-through after opposing exits
abstain: break alone without buildup

concepts.name: Dominant pressure
concepts.definition: Relative swing structure and correction behavior identify the side currently controlling the chart.
cues: higher highs/lows or lower highs/lows
corrections fail to cross significant prior swings
abstain: first counter swing against a strong move

concepts.name: Support and resistance
concepts.definition: Prior reaction levels are information; after a break they may reverse role on a retest.
cues: repeated reactions
role reversal on retest
abstain: blind fade
blind breakout chase

concepts.name: Buildup / pre-breakout tension
concepts.definition: Alternating bars push and bounce in a compact range at the boundary under attack; the buildup should provide a technically defensible signal bar and protection level for the break.
cues: tight cluster
boundary fight
defensible signal bar and stop
protection just beyond the last distinctive buildup high/low
abstain: no buildup
buildup away from boundary
technical protection requires an unusually wide stop

concepts.name: False break
concepts.definition: A poorly prepared pattern break reverses or is undone; classify from setup conditions rather than outcome.
cues: instant reversal
break undone after weak participation
abstain: do not infer quality from hindsight

concepts.name: Tease break
concepts.definition: A slightly premature break may retreat inside the range, test an internal level, and later re-break.
cues: partial follow-through
internal ceiling/floor test
second attempt
abstain: tight stop vulnerable to first retreat

concepts.name: False high / low
concepts.definition: A single-bar break fails and the opposite bar breaks back; at key levels it can foreshadow pressure in the opposite direction.
cues: failed neighboring-bar break
subsequent opposite break
abstain: wait for a later buildup

concepts.name: Pullback reversal
concepts.definition: A price correction against a dominant swing reaches the EMA25 area and preferably a technical support/resistance test, prepares a turn, then breaks a separate signal bar in the original pressure direction. Time corrections may instead resemble pattern-break variants.
cues: measure retracement from where the latest dominant swing began; source guidance is usually 50-60%, sometimes 40% in a strong trend
correction bars should on average be no wider than dominant-swing bars; watch reluctant progress against pressure
wait for the EMA25 area and preferably a prior technical test before treating a turn as ready
distinguish a one-bar turnaround, extra buildup and a possible second break in an M/W turn
distinguish trending continuation from a wider range; a local dominant leg can still point into a range boundary
abstain: a pullback-line break alone before EMA25 or a technical test is insufficient
aggressive correction with a modest first turnaround and too little fighting
opposing wider dominance, an adverse magnet or poor technical protection

The local version3 proxy uses bounded 5-8-bar dominant legs, 2-8-bar price corrections, a 40-bar EMA estimate and subsequent close confirmation. An optional first-close-break / opposing-return / second-close-break sequence is a local M/W proxy. Exact bounds and wick proximity are local choices; wider trend/range selection and the complete source method remain unimplemented.
a reversal requiring passage through a range barrier, competing wider structure, or continuation near the far end of a range calls for greater selectivity

concepts.name: Ceiling test / magnet
concepts.definition: An internal floor or ceiling of an arch/range can attract a pullback and become a bounce or re-break platform.
cues: last internal level
role reversal
test before outer-boundary attack
abstain: outer boundary entry while nearer magnet is untested

concepts.name: Round-number effect
concepts.definition: 00/50 levels on the reference EUR/USD 5-minute chart act as recurring battle zones and magnets; low volatility may shift attention to 20 levels.
cues: fight around round level
favorable or adverse magnet
abstain: assume automatic rejection or break

concepts.name: Signal bar and entry bar
concepts.definition: The final buildup bar defines a candidate trigger; the later bar that breaks it is the entry bar. A setup-close measurement is a different study policy.
cues: boundary under attack with alternating-bar buildup
bullish signal bar near the upper boundary or bearish bar near the lower boundary
subsequent break, with pressure, protection and obstacles checked beforehand
abstain: front-running the signal-bar break
confusing a chart close or isolated shape with a source entry

concepts.name: Pattern break combi
concepts.definition: A directional powerbar and neighbouring inside bar compress tension within a larger breakout context; the inside-bar break usually times the entry. Variants require context rather than mechanical acceptance.
cues: powerbar direction agrees with surrounding pressure
inside bar located toward the directional end of the powerbar
second inside bar may add tension; matching color or equal extremes are preferences, not requirements
abstain: isolated inside bar without a qualifying breakout context
mistaking a long inactive sideways phase for active buildup
The local close-confirmed proxy excludes reversed/doji variants and bars touching both the break and opposite protection. Its numerical thresholds are not book prescriptions.

concepts.name: Bracket, target, stop and costs
concepts.definition: The book illustrates full-position entry and an OCO target/stop bracket on EURUSD M5. Its 20/10 pip example is contextual and must be reassessed for range, costs and execution.
cues: entry, protective stop and target defined before outcome
market-stop slippage and spread/commission recorded
reassess distances when volatility changes
abstain: copying EURUSD pip distances into XAUUSD
treating an OHLC touch as a guaranteed fill
regarding the app 2.2/1 ATR study as the book's bracket

concepts.name: News report exit
concepts.definition: Upcoming material releases can disrupt the pressure visible before them. The source discusses declining exposure or leaving a trade before the release, with timing dependent on the event and context.
cues: dated event schedule and relevance to the instrument
quiet pre-release action may still precede a large response
record the exit decision before observing the news outcome
abstain: inferring a scheduled release from candles alone
applying an invented universal countdown or safe lead time

concepts.name: Resistance exit and room to target
concepts.definition: Identify an obstruction and possible reduced objective before entry, then assess whether the remaining room justifies the trade. Compare intervention with leaving the original bracket alone.
cues: range boundary, round number, prior extreme or technical test ahead
distinguish trending from ranging conditions
source example discusses 14 pip room with a 20/10 bracket, not a universal instrument threshold
abstain: lowering the target after entry out of fear
insufficient room after costs
claiming every touched resistance must reject

concepts.name: Reversal exit and adverse buildup
concepts.definition: An established trade can face an adverse M/W-type cluster. A break supported by adverse powerbar pressure may justify a source-style exit; a weak flag perforation can instead be a trap.
cues: middle-part cluster with failed progress toward target
adverse powerbar or combi followed by its break
record how much of the prior move existed before the reversal
abstain: using any counter-colored bar as an exit
confusing a newly failed breakout with a profitable trade reversing
inventing intrabar order from an OHLC candle

concepts.name: Trade selection and trading breaks for failure
concepts.definition: Evaluate pressure and conditions before the local setup. A well-formed break against dominance may later fail and offer a counterbreak with dominance; a false break alone is insufficient.
cues: boundary, buildup and signal in the attempted break
counterbreak aligns with established dominance
check overhead/underfoot resistance, EMA distance and adverse magnets
abstain: fading every failed breakout
aggressive pullback pressure or frantic unusually large bars
entry with too little buildup or no room to travel

concepts.definition: The source presents March-August 2012 EURUSD sessions as a study corpus, using context across consecutive days. Chart annotations and educational outcomes are not a machine-labelled XAUUSD validation set.
cues: review the whole session including skipped and ambiguous cases
source labels pb/pbp/pbc/pr/tff distinguish setup families
record session timezone separately from UTC market data
abstain: turning annotated historical examples into a reported strategy win rate

concepts.name: Trade size and compounding
concepts.definition: Sizing changes the accounting outcome of an existing sequence of trades. Percentage-based adjustments scale units with capital; they do not improve the underlying trade-selection edge.
cues: separate trade result in risk units from currency accounting
reduce units as the model account shrinks
source numerical growth examples are hypothetical illustrations
abstain: projecting the book's smooth example growth as a forecast
increasing size to compensate for an unprofitable method
ignoring minimum lot size, costs or execution losses

concepts.name: Adapting to low volatility
concepts.definition: Persistent low activity can weaken follow-through even when the price-action principles remain relevant. The source considers smaller objectives, more selective continuation trades and alternative markets or frames.
cues: compare activity and follow-through with the tested baseline
require meaningful buildup rather than motionless bars
source 200-tick adaptation needs genuine tick data; this app remains XAUUSD M5
abstain: forcing daily trades in a stale environment
synthesizing ticks or a faster chart from M5 OHLC
automatically shortening targets without testing costs and context

concepts.name: Pattern break
concepts.definition: A repeatedly tested pattern boundary comes under pressure from compact alternating buildup. A directional signal bar near that boundary sets a reference for the subsequent entry-bar break; pressure, protection and obstacles still govern context.
cues: dominant pressure agrees with the intended break
several alternating bars compress against a repeatedly tested boundary
signal bar and subsequent breakout bar have separate identities
technical protection must be defensible before the break
abstain: an isolated boundary perforation without prepared buildup
buildup away from the barrier or a premature tease break
opposing dominance, obstructed room or excessive technical protection distance
The local horizontal four-to-six-bar close-confirmed proxy is narrower than the source. Its numerical thresholds, lack of wider context and ATR outcome study are explicit limitations.

concepts.name: Pattern break pullback
concepts.definition: After a pattern boundary breaks, price may cling to the broken barrier or follow through and return to test it. A new signal bar in the barrier and EMA25 area can frame a second-instance entry in the original break direction; the initial break need not have been a tradable regular setup.
cues: distinguish an initial boundary break from a later post-break signal
a hanging barrier fight and a return after excursion are separate variants
prefer a signal testing both the broken barrier and the EMA25 area
the stronger the pullback, the more buildup may be needed to force a turn
inspect correction depth, opposing powerbars and additional inside-bar tension at the turn; a gentle angular correction differs from a blocky fight
abstain: initial break fully undone or signal formed before a barrier/EMA test
strong V-shaped correction without sufficient evidence of a turn
adverse magnets, opposing dominance or excessive technical protection distance

Local horizontal one-to-six-bar close-confirmed variants use a bounded SMA25-seeded EMA25 estimate. Numerical thresholds, limited wider context and the ATR outcome study do not implement the complete source method.

concepts.name: Obstacles and room ahead
concepts.definition: Examine prior resistance above a bullish break or support below a bearish break, the technical protection distance and adverse magnets before interpreting the setup. Nearby swing resistance can leave little room even when the turnaround bar looks attractive; apparent room alone cannot establish a trade.
cues: assess direction, ranging or trending conditions, and nearby obstacles before participation
compare available room with technically defensible protection, rather than widening the stop to hope
distinguish geometric context known at the setup from later follow-through
an EMA is an average, not support or resistance by itself
abstain: a neat signal bar positioned immediately against prior swing resistance or support
a wide technical stop or adverse magnet undermining the setup
declaring the path clear because a bounded scan finds no confirmed swing
The app offers an optional local context measurement, not a standalone signal detector or filtered win-rate. Two-sided swings, 96-bar scope, zone tolerance and XAUUSD round landmarks are local rules.

source_lenses.definition: The source asks whether a local correction or continuation agrees with the wider trend, sits inside a range, or is approaching the far boundary where opposing structure can dominate. This is a review lens for selecting and skipping examples, not a mechanical detector rule.
cues: compare the local swing with the wider trend or range context
check competing structure and the nearest range boundary before treating a continuation as attractive
record when a local pullback turn points into an adverse wider level
abstain: do not infer a universal trend/range cutoff from the source figures
withhold a selection claim when the wider context or competing structure is unavailable

source_lenses.name: Trading breaks for failure
source_lenses.definition: A reversal break against dominant pressure can fail and later offer a counterbreak once price reclaims the relevant broken barrier. The source treats this as a selective context review: the first reversal attempt in a fresh dominant swing differs from a later, blockier structure that has had time to mature.
cues: a reversal break points into a trending 25EMA; compare it with a continuation break away from the average

abstain: do not fade every failed breakout or call any higher low or lower high a failure entry
a late barrier reclaim does not by itself restore the earlier dominant edge
do not infer a universal attempt count, time threshold, profitability or executable intrabar entry from the printed examples

book_index.summary: Preparation and personal study precede methodology adoption. Build a database of context and recurring price behaviour; no shortcut establishes an edge.

book_index.title: Price Action Principles - Theory
book_index.summary: Pressure, defended boundaries, tension, false/tease breaks, pullbacks and magnets form the core vocabulary; its theory overview and false-break discussion emphasize assessing preparation, participation and context before acting.

book_index.title: Price Action Principles - Practice
book_index.summary: Visually reviewed printed pp. 33-65 and the blank divider at p. 66: selective pressure and EMA context, false breaks, buildup and squeeze, W/M and flag variants, technical tests, magnets, room, barrier placement, powerbars and inside-bar confluence. Source examples distinguish exit pressure from countertrend entry and do not supply measured XAUUSD outcomes.

book_index.title: Orders, Target and Stop
book_index.summary: Illustrative EURUSD bracket and order mechanics, slippage, cost models and periodic reassessment of distances. Printed p. 72 is a visually confirmed blank divider.

book_index.title: Trade Setups
book_index.summary: Four named setup families: pattern break, pattern break pullback, pattern break combi and pullback reversal. All interval pages have source review notes, including blank142. Notes retain pressure, signal/entry timing, technical protection, magnets, flag/pole harmony, range context and selective EMA25 exceptions; source review does not establish detector completeness or measured outcomes.

book_index.title: Manual Exits
book_index.summary: News, preplanned resistance objectives and adverse reversal development are distinct reasons for intervention; reviewed pages also distinguish slippage/news risk, proactive resistance exits, source-specific range/trend checks, and outcome-blind comparison with the untouched bracket.

book_index.title: Skipping Trades and Trading Breaks for Failure
book_index.summary: Context can invalidate an otherwise tidy setup. Barrier reclaim, first versus mature reversal attempts, technical support, correction strength and proportional buildup distinguish selective failure trades from indiscriminately fading breaks. The reviewed Ww/Mm and supertrend examples are source-only narrative evidence; p.210 is a blank divider.

book_index.title: Recap Part 1
book_index.summary: The full printed pp. 211-244 interval is reviewed: recap principles and Figures 8.1-8.14 assess whole-chart pressure, obstruction, correction strength, buildup harmony, discretionary exits and patience without prediction. Printed pp. 242 and 244 are visually confirmed blank; p. 243 is the Part 2 Evaluation and Management divider. Narrative examples remain source-only, with no detector or measured-outcome claim.

book_index.title: Consecutive Intraday Charts
book_index.summary: March-August 2012 session corpus and its annotation vocabulary. Introductory pages 245-249 and charts 250-381 have reviewed source notes; printed 272 is the April 2 plate despite the March running header. Printed p. 382 is a visually confirmed blank divider with no OCR or concept anchor. Calendar-month ranges remain navigation references and individual chart outcomes remain untranscribed.

book_index.title: Trade Size - Compounding
book_index.summary: Account arithmetic and unit changes are separated from technical selection. Example growth paths do not forecast returns.

book_index.title: Adapting to Low Volatility
book_index.summary: Adaptation discusses strategic selectivity, objectives, multiple markets and genuine tick frames. The reviewed box examples stress buildup, round-number magnets, room and technical protection; the current product scope stays one XAUUSD M5 chart.

book_index.title: Final Words
book_index.summary: The closing page returns to study and establishing an edge before committing capital.
